'''Ignas''' "'''Iggy'''" '''Brazdeikis''' (born January 8, 1999) is a Lithuanian-born Canadian [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. Brazdeikis is a right-handed athlete who shoots left-handed in basketball. He has represented the Canadian national teams in junior levels. During the season, he established a Michigan record by earning four Big Ten Freshmen of the week awards and was included on both the [[John Wooden Award]] Midseason Top 25 and Late Season Top 20 watchlists. As a freshman, he was a [[2018–19 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2019]] Second team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] selection, the Big Ten Freshman of the Year and a Big Ten All-Freshman honoree.

==Early life==
Brazdeikis was born in [[Kaunas]], [[Lithuania]], to Diana and Sigitas "Sigis" Brazdeikis. He has an older sister, Ema. His second aunt, Lina Brazdeikytė, is a former professional basketball player who won the [[EuroBasket Women 1997]] with the [[Lithuania women's national basketball team|Lithuania women's national team]].<ref name="LTU heritage">{{cite web |last1=Augustis |first1=Mindaugas |title=J. Valančiūno pašonėje bręstantis talentas: planuose – NBA, kraujyje – Lietuvos rinktinė |url=https://www.delfi.lt/krepsinis/herojai/j-valanciuno-pasoneje-brestantis-talentas-planuose-nba-kraujyje-lietuvos-rinktine.d?id=74287990 |website=DELFI |accessdate=December 3, 2018 |language=lt-LT |date=April 10, 2017}}</ref> His family emigrated to [[Chicago]] before moving to [[Winnipeg]] and [[Etobicoke]] before settling in [[Oakville, Ontario]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2018/10/27/michigan-basketball-ignas-brazdeikis/1774602002/|title=Meet Ignas Brazdeikis: 'There hasn't been a Michigan player like me'|accessdate=December 3, 2018|date=October 27, 2018|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|author=Sang, Orion}}</ref>

==High school career==
Brazdeikis was the Ontario Scholastic Basketball Association MVP in 2017 and 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/OntarioSBA/status/852186232625016833|title=@OntarioSBA status update|accessdate=April 2, 2018|date=April 12, 2017|publisher=[[Twitter]]|author=Ontario Scholastic Basketball Association}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/OntarioSBA/status/974657856937934849|title=@OntarioSBA status update|accessdate=April 2, 2018|date=March 16, 2018|publisher=[[Twitter]]|author=Ontario Scholastic Basketball Association}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ontariosba.ca/news_article/show/898170?referrer_id=3072240|title=Men's 2018 OSBA Award Winners Announced|website=ontariosba.ca|date=March 16, 2018|access-date=April 3, 2018}}</ref> As a junior he led Orangeville to the 2017 OSBA championship and won the tournament MVP award.<ref name=TIPAFESfW/> Brazdeikis is generally right-handed, including his [[dribble]], but shoots the basketball left-handed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.landof10.com/michigan/michigan-basketball-ignas-brazdeikis-recruiting-scorer-canadian|title=Michigan signee Ignas Brazdeikis is different, but he’s right fit for Wolverines, John Beilein|accessdate=April 2, 2018|date=March 28, 2018|website=landof10.com|publisher=[[Cox Media Group]]|author=Goheen, Kevin}}</ref> During Brazdeikis's high school years, he was mentored by former Wolverine [[Nik Stauskas]].<ref name=IBhtbMlisfMW/>

By May 2017 Brazdeikis was undecided between matriculating with the class of 2017 or 2018 and had taken unofficial visits to Michigan, Vanderbilt and Cincinnati.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.zagsblog.com/2017/05/05/canadian-guard-ignas-brazdeikis-leaning-toward-2018/|title=Canadian Wing Ignas Brazdeikis ‘Leaning Toward’ 2018|accessdate=April 2, 2018|date=May 5, 2017|author=Zagoria, Adam|website=Zagsblog.com}}</ref> After accumulating offers from several schools including Baylor, Cal, Illinois, Oklahoma, Oregon, Tennessee, and USC and rankings of number 66 overall and 16 small forward at 247sports.com, Brazdeikis announced that he would officially visit Michigan, Vanderbilt and Florida on September 8, 15 and 29, 2017, respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thespun.com/college-hoops/ignas-brazdeikis-michigan-vanderbilt-florida-official-visits|title=4-Star F Ignas Brazdeikis Sets Up 3 Official Visits|accessdate=April 2, 2018|date=September 8, 2017|work=The Spun|author=}}</ref> He gave a Michigan a verbal commitment on September 22.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2722376-4-star-sg-prospect-ignas-brazdeikis-commits-to-michigan-over-vanderbilt|title=4-Star SG Prospect Ignas Brazdeikis Commits to Michigan over Vanderbilt|accessdate=April 2, 2018|date=September 22, 2017|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|author=Wells, Adam}}</ref> After he committed, Michigan stopped recruiting [[R. J. Barrett]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2017/r-j-barrett-final-three-decision-date-set|title=The R.J. Barrett Blog: Final three, decision date set and more|accessdate=April 2, 2018|date=October 6, 2017|work=[[USA Today]]|author=Barrett, R. J.}}</ref> He signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] with Michigan on November 10, 2017 along with the 2018 class that included Colin Castleton, David DeJulius, Brandon Johns, and Adrien Nunez.<ref name=TIPAFESfW/>

Brazdeikis was expected to be Michigan's best incoming freshman according to [[Yahoo Sports]] and [[ESPN]] in 2018.<ref name=Wt2ft2cbs>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/way-early-top-25-2018-19-college-basketball-season-033644755.html|title=Way-too-early top 25 for the 2018–19 college basketball season|accessdate=April 3, 2018|date=April 2, 2018|publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]]|author=Eisenberg, Jeff}}</ref><ref name=FoFFKlWT2f2>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22966716/college-basketball-way-too-early-top-25-rankings-2018-19|title=Fresh off Final Four, Kansas leads Way-Too-Early Top 25 for 2018–19|accessdate=April 3, 2018|date=April 2, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Medcalf, Myron}}</ref>

==National team career==
Brazdeikis earned a silver medal with Team Canada at the [[2015 FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]], averaging 9.2 points and 7.2 rebounds a game. He also played for Canada at the [[2016 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]], averaging 14.7 points and 6.9 rebounds a game.<ref name=TIPAFESfW>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2017/11/10/mens-basketball-two-in-state-products-among-five-early-signees-for-wolverines.aspx?path=mbball|title=Two In-State Products Among Five Early Signees for Wolverines|accessdate=April 2, 2018|date=November 10, 2017|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]}}</ref> He was invited to participate in the April 13, 2018, [[Nike Hoop Summit]]<ref name=IBhtbMlisfMW>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/bigten/2018/04/11/michigan-recruit-iggy-brazdeikis-international-success-following-moritz-wagner/507386002/|title=Iggy Brazeikis hopes to be Michigan's latest international success following Moritz Wagner|accessdate=April 13, 2018|date=April 11, 2018|work=[[USA Today]]|author=Schnell, Lindsay}}</ref> and posted 9 points, 4 rebounds and 3 assists in 12:16 of playing time during the 89–76 World team victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2018/04/hsum-game.aspx|title=World Select Team Wins 2018 Nike Hoop Summit 89-76 (box score link)|accessdate=April 16, 2018|date=April 13, 2018|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}}</ref>
